summary: stage.* client messages are dispatched with NO role check; a mobile conn can drive stage-only actions (playback device hijack, forced round transitions).
code:
case protocol.CMsgStagePlayerState:
		e.onStagePlayerState(connID, env)
	case protocol.CMsgStageDeviceReady:
		e.onStageDeviceReady(connID, env)
scenario: The dispatch role gate at lines 461-475 covers only admin.* types. A hostile mobile (role=mobile, never sent the stage/admin secret) sends {"t":"stage.deviceReady","d":{"spotifyDeviceID":"<attacker-device>"}} -> onStageDeviceReady calls e.audio.SetDevice(attackerDevice), rerouting every subsequent Play/Pause/Resume Web-API call to a device the attacker controls (or a bogus ID => NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE, killing playback). It can also send {"t":"stage.playerState","d":{"trackEnded":true}}: in KARAOKE that triggers beginTransition() (skips the whole skip-vote), in ROUND_ACTIVE it triggers endRound() (kills the live round). None of this requires the stage/admin secret.
suggested_fix: Gate stage.* the same way admin.* is gated: in dispatch, require role==RoleStage (or RoleStage||RoleAdmin) before calling onStagePlayerState/onStageDeviceReady, and sendError("forbidden") otherwise.

summary: Buzz ordering is determined by command-channel enqueue order (goroutine scheduling), not the stamped server arrival time; arrivalMs and EffectiveBuzzTime are computed then discarded, violating §4B/§4C.
code:
_ = anticheat.EffectiveBuzzTime(arrivalMs, p.RTTMs)

	won, err := e.lock.TryAcquire(context.Background(), e.roundKey, p.ID)
scenario: §4B requires arrivalUnixMs to be the ONLY ordering input, and §4C requires latency compensation. Here the effective time is thrown away (assigned to _), and the winner is simply whichever buzz command reaches the Run loop first. Between the transport's arrival stamp and e.submit() enqueue, N connection goroutines race, so a buzz stamped earlier (lower arrivalMs, e.g. a higher-latency-compensated player) can be enqueued and win the lock AFTER a later-arriving buzz. Single-winner still holds, but the earliest/fairest buzz is not guaranteed to win, and RTT compensation never applies.
suggested_fix: Order buzzes by EffectiveBuzzTime (arrivalMs adjusted by capped RTT). E.g. within ROUND_ACTIVE, briefly collect contending buzzes or record the effective time on the lock and resolve the winner by min(effectiveTime) rather than pure enqueue order; at minimum stop discarding EffectiveBuzzTime.

summary: Daily-double can deadlock in DAILY_DOUBLE state: a rater disconnecting (or refusing to rate) shrinks ratingPool but never re-evaluates the completion condition, so finishDailyDouble is never called.
scenario: enterDailyDouble builds ratingPool={A,B}; finishDailyDouble only fires when len(ratings) >= len(ratingPool) (line 1299). A rates (ratings={A}), then B disconnects: OnDisconnect deletes ratingPool[B] -> ratingPool={A}, but only re-checks skip votes when state==KARAOKE, never the daily-double completion. Now len(ratings)==1==len(ratingPool) yet finishDailyDouble is never invoked -> the game is stuck in DAILY_DOUBLE until an admin manually endRound/reveal. Equivalently, hostile mobiles that simply never send 'rate' hang the phase indefinitely (no timeout).
suggested_fix: In OnDisconnect (and onAdminKick), when e.state==StateDailyDouble re-evaluate completion: if len(e.ratings) >= len(e.ratingPool) call finishDailyDouble() (or enterKaraoke() if ratingPool becomes empty). Also add an AutoKaraoke-style timeout for DAILY_DOUBLE so refusal-to-rate cannot stall the game.

summary: Every heartbeat (any role, unauthenticated, no nonce, no rate limit) forces a full telemetry + O(players^2) cheat-report rebuild on the single Run goroutine.
scenario: onHeartbeat runs on the single Run loop and unconditionally calls broadcastTelemetry(), which builds telemetryData() (O(P)) AND cheatReportData(). cheatReportData calls playerIP() per mobile player, each iterating that player's conns, i.e. ~O(P * conns) plus the shared-IP map pass. A hostile mobile spams heartbeat frames as fast as the socket allows; each one is enqueued and executed serially, monopolizing the Run goroutine that also handles buzz/grade/reveal. With a moderate player count this starves the game loop (buzzes/grades delayed) — a cheap client-side flood DoS.
suggested_fix: Rate-limit heartbeat-driven telemetry (e.g. coalesce to at most once per ~1-2s via a dirty flag consumed by the existing 60s ticker) instead of rebuilding+broadcasting on every heartbeat; and/or throttle inbound heartbeats per connection at the transport edge.

summary: admin.award applies an unvalidated Delta directly to a player's score (no range clamp, negative or huge values accepted, integer overflow possible).
scenario: Requires the admin secret, so lower severity, but the handoff explicitly calls for validation here. A delta of math.MaxInt or a huge negative value is applied verbatim (p.Score += d.Delta), yielding absurd/negative scores or wrap-around, then persisted and broadcast. Unlike onAdminSetThresh (clamped 50-100) and onRate (1-5), award has no bounds check.
suggested_fix: Clamp d.Delta to a sane per-action range (e.g. [-1000,1000]) and clamp the resulting p.Score to a floor of 0 (or a documented min) before persisting/broadcasting.

summary: resolvePlayer stores the client-supplied Handle verbatim with no length/content limit; it is then broadcast to every connection in scoreboard/telemetry/lockout frames.
scenario: A hostile mobile sends a hello with a Handle up to the transport frame cap (~1MiB) of arbitrary/unicode/control bytes. It is stored and then echoed in scoreboardData() to ALL roles on every score change and in SMsgLockout {ByHandle} to all mobiles on every buzz. A ~1MiB handle amplified across every scoreboard broadcast to N connections is a bandwidth/CPU amplification DoS, and unsanitized control/unicode can corrupt stage/admin rendering. No max length or sanitization is applied anywhere on the engine surface.
suggested_fix: In resolvePlayer, clamp Handle to a small max (e.g. 24 runes) and strip control characters before assigning; reject/truncate rather than store arbitrary-length input.

summary: submit's 'backpressure' fallback does not run inline as its comment claims; the default branch issues the identical blocking channel send, so when the loop is saturated the calling goroutine simply blocks.
scenario: The comment promises 'run inline only if the loop is saturated', but the default case performs the same blocking send e.cmds <- command{...}. If the 256-deep buffer fills (e.g. the Run loop is stalled in a synchronous lock.TryAcquire against a hung Redis while a heartbeat/buzz flood arrives), every connection goroutine calling OnConnect/OnMessage/OnDisconnect blocks indefinitely instead of getting any relief — the fallback is a no-op that only obscures the stall.
suggested_fix: Either drop the misleading default branch and document that submit applies blocking backpressure, or implement real relief (bounded blocking with a timeout/context, or execute fn synchronously only when it is safe to do so from a non-Run goroutine — which currently it is not).
